title: Our Lady of the Rosary
short_summary: Our Lady of the Rosary is a title of the Blessed Virgin Mary associated with the Rosary, a meditative prayer centered on the life, death, and Resurrection of Jesus Christ. The October 7 memorial developed from the Christian victory at Lepanto in 1571 and from the long growth of Rosary devotion.
key_facts: The U.S. calendar keeps Our Lady of the Rosary as a memorial on October 7.
The Rosary developed gradually during the second millennium, and Dominican preachers helped shape and spread its familiar form.
A commonly used Rosary consists of five decades of vocal prayer joined to meditation on mysteries from the lives of Jesus and Mary.
Saint John Paul II proposed the Luminous Mysteries in 2002 alongside the traditional Joyful, Sorrowful, and Glorious Mysteries.

sections.heading: Origins and development
sections.body: The Rosary took shape over centuries from the Christian practice of repeating familiar prayers while meditating on the mysteries of salvation. Medieval forms were called Marian Psalters because sets of Hail Marys offered a pattern corresponding to the 150 Psalms. By the late Middle Ages, Dominican preachers such as Blessed Alan de la Roche were organizing Rosary confraternities and promoting the devotion across Europe.

sections.heading: Dominican tradition
sections.body: Catholic tradition closely associates the Rosary with Saint Dominic and the Order of Preachers. Its modern form developed after Dominic's lifetime, but Dominicans played a central role in its organization and spread. The Rosary became characteristic of Dominican life and united contemplation of Christ with the Order's work of preaching.

sections.heading: Lepanto and the memorial
sections.body: In 1571 Pope Pius V asked Christians to pray the Rosary while the Holy League confronted the Ottoman fleet at Lepanto. The victory on October 7 was attributed to Mary's intercession. Pius established a feast of Our Lady of Victory, and Gregory XIII later gave it the title Our Lady of the Rosary. Clement XI extended the celebration to the universal Church, and Pius X fixed October 7 as its date.

sections.heading: Prayers and mysteries
sections.body: Each decade combines an Our Father, ten Hail Marys, and a Glory Be with meditation on a Gospel mystery. The Joyful Mysteries concern Christ's infancy, the Luminous Mysteries his public ministry, the Sorrowful Mysteries his Passion, and the Glorious Mysteries his Resurrection and the life of the Church.

catholic_connection_sections.heading: A Christ-centered Marian prayer
catholic_connection_sections.body: The Hail Mary gives the Rosary its Marian form, but Jesus is the center of every mystery. Catholics pray with Mary while contemplating her Son from the Annunciation through the Resurrection and the sending of the Holy Spirit.

catholic_connection_sections.heading: Scripture and contemplation
catholic_connection_sections.body: The mysteries provide a framework for returning repeatedly to the events of the Gospel. Repetition supplies a steady rhythm while the mind attends to Christ's words and deeds.

historical_cautions: The traditional account of Mary personally giving the Rosary to Saint Dominic appears in sources written well after his death. Describe it as Catholic or Dominican tradition rather than a securely dated event.
